2607.17712.title: Learning to Detect Cross-Modal Negation: An Analysis of Latent Representations and an Attention-Based Solution
2607.17712.paper_summary: Detecting high-level semantic concepts like negation across modalities remains a challenge for current multimodal systems. We analyze this as a fundamental representation learning problem, providing the first evidence that negation does not form a linearly or non-linearly separable class in the latent spaces of standard vision-language models (VLMs). We demonstrate that pretrained embeddings primarily encode modality-specific features, lacking a generalizable negation signal. To overcome this, we propose a novel cross-modal attention architecture that explicitly models inter-modal dependencies, achieving performance gains of up to +7.03% F1 over unimodal baselines. Our analysis reveals a key asymmetry: while textual negation often appears independently, visual negation is semantically dependent on linguistic context, a finding validated through our statistical analysis of 3,222 political video-text pairs automatically annotated via \textsc{Qwen2.5-VL}. By combining this analysis with self-supervised video representations (JEPA2), we advance the modeling of temporal negation. This work provides new methods and insights for learning robust, semantically-aligned representations in multimodal systems.
2607.17712.paper_summary_zh: 偵測像否定這樣的高階語意概念在不同模態之間仍然是當前多模態系統的一大挑戰。<lb/>我們將此分析為一個基本的表示學習問題，提供首個證據表明否定在標準視覺-語言模型（VLMs）的潛在空間中並不形成線性或非線性可分的類別。<lb/>我們證明預訓練的嵌入主要編碼模態特定的特徵，缺乏可泛化的否定信號。<lb/>為了克服這一點，我們提出了一種新穎的跨模態注意力架構，明確建模模態間的依賴關係，實現了比單模態基準高出最多 +7.03% 的 F1 性能提升。<lb/>我們的分析揭示了一個關鍵的不對稱性：雖然文本否定通常獨立出現，但視覺否定在語義上依賴於語言上下文，這一發現通過我們對 3,222 對政治視頻-文本進行的統計分析得到了驗證，這些對是通過 \textsc{Qwen2.5-VL} 自動標註的。<lb/>通過將這一分析與自監督視頻表示（JEPA2）相結合，我們推進了時間否定的建模。<lb/>這項工作為在多模態系統中學習穩健的、語義對齊的表示提供了新的方法和見解。
